records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Internal dispatch-desk reconciliation tool for mismatched references, where operators compared an overnight spreadsheet with a daily export. Personally built with Python and SQL, with a Python parser and SQL checks, and used Git and PostgreSQL. Supervisors wanted understandable exceptions; the team preferred visible warnings for late source files and kept empty rows visible. The supervisor made final dispatch decisions. The reported improvement was a team result, not solely attributable to Ada.

records.title: Reconciliation time reduction
records.subtitle: Team result at Harbor Tools
records.summary: Dispatch Loom reduced reconciliation time from 5 hours to 2 hours per week, measured over six weekly runs. This was a team result; Ada’s stated contribution was the parser and checks, and coworkers also changed their checking habits. Delivery speed was not measured; an earlier 50% time-saved figure was corrected as wrong.

decisions.reason: The profile and its professional-use and employment denials are supported by the source; the technology-use claims are also corroborated by the work and skills described.
The employer, role, employment dates, personal project work, and training and handbook claims are supported by the transcript.
The project description, aliases, tools, operational context, responsibilities, supervisor decision-making, and team-level outcome are supported and preserve the source’s qualifications.
The source supports personally training 12 coworkers in two workshops and writing the handbook; it also says exact workshop dates are unavailable.
The record reports the corrected reconciliation-time measurement, identifies it as a team result, distinguishes it from delivery speed, and notes the correction to the earlier 50% figure.
The source supports personal use of Python to build the Dispatch Loom parser and places Python in the Data tools category.
The source supports personal use of SQL to write the Dispatch Loom checks and places SQL in the Data tools category.
The source supports using PostgreSQL for the production database and places it in the Data tools category.
The source supports using Git for version control and places it in the Collaboration category.
The source supports coworker training and a plain-language handbook, and places coworker training in the Collaboration category.
The degree, institution, and attendance dates match the source.

The source explicitly calls this a fictional certificate, but the record presents it as an earned certification without preserving that material qualification. Calling it course completion rather than a professional license does not resolve the omission.
